Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Greenville-Spartanburg SC
223 AM EST Fri Nov 27 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
Wind gusts were increased slightly for today, but should remain 
below Wind Advisory criteria.

Aviation discussion updated for the 06z TAFs.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
1. Gusty winds will continue across the area today, diminishing
later this evening. Light wintry precipitation is also expected
to continue near the Tennessee border, with some accumulations
likely, mainly over the higher elevations.
2. Temperatures warm quickly this weekend ahead of the next cold
front. The front is expected to bring rain and more gusty winds
to our area Sunday into early Monday.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Key message 1: Gusty winds will continue across the area today, 
diminishing later this evening. Light wintry precipitation is 
also expected to continue near the Tennessee border, with some 
accumulations likely, mainly over the higher elevations.

A sprawling upper low/attendant trough currently centered over 
the TN Valley will lift NE into the central Appalachians this 
morning. The associated sfc low will continue to lift northward
and away from our CWA, but the sfc pressure gradient will remain 
tight across our area resulting in more gusty SW winds. The gusty 
winds will continue thru the day today and weaken this evening. 
The main caveat will be over the NC mtns, where gusts are expected 
to strengthen a bit more this evening and into early Sat. We still 
expect wind speeds to remain just below Wind Advisory criteria, 
nonetheless peak wind gusts of 30 to 40 mph are anticipated today 
across most of our lower terrain with occasional higher gusts 
possible. Above 3500 ft and especially over the northern NC mtns, 
gusts greater than 40 mph appear more likely later tonight thru 
early Sat. Winds this strong will be capable of blowing around 
loose objects and may cause localized power outages. 

Precipitation chances remain in the likely/categorical range across 
portions of the NC mtns thru the overnight and morning as a defor-
mation zone lingers over the western part of our CWA. The potential
for additional wintry precip remains high, mainly across the higher 
elevations, with some light wintry mix possibly reaching the valley 
floors around daybreak this morning. Due to the track of the main low
pressure system, low-level flow in the cold advection regime is fcst
to remain mostly W/SW. As a result, upslope lift should be minimal,
and most of the rising motion will be generally due to synoptic forcing. 
However, the SWLY flow will likely result in a small area of upslope
enhancement across southwest NC with accumulating snowfall on the order
of 1 to 3 inches (with localized higher amounts possible) across the 
higher elevations of western Graham and Macon Counties through this 
morning. This is expected to be insufficient for a Winter Wx Advisory, 
but a Special Weather Statement (SPS) highlighting the potential for 
some slick high elevation roads appears warranted. While mostly snow
and/or rain is expected, model fcst soundings continue to develop at 
least a weak warm nose across the southern Appalachians early this 
morning, so light freezing rain or drizzle is possible across our NC 
counties bordering TN, and even within the valleys. Any ice accums
should be negligible.


Key message 2: Temperatures warm quickly this weekend ahead of the 
next cold front. The front is expected to bring rain and more gusty 
winds to our area Sunday into early Monday.

A strengthening upper shortwave trof is expected to eject out of
the central Plains and across the TN and OH Valleys on Sunday, with 
an associated deepening sfc low approaching our area from the west. 
The attendant fast-moving cold front is still on track to move thru
our CWA late Sunday into early Monday, with sufficient Gulf inflow 
and low-level forcing to support categorical PoPs across the entire 
area late Sunday. Expected rainfall amounts have trended a bit higher
across the western half of our CWA, with QPF of roughly 0.5 to 0.75"
fcst, and roughly 0.1 to 0.4" still expected across the east. As such,
the excessive rainfall/flooding threat appears minimal.  

Temperatures warm quickly over the weekend within the warm advection 
ahead of the front. This should ensure all precipitation falls as 
liquid, although a brief period of NW flow/upslope snow showers will 
be possible across the higher elevations along the NC/TN border late 
Sunday night/early Monday. Dry conditions are otherwise expected Monday 
thru Thursday, with temperatures near normal for Monday and Tuesday and
warming above normal by Wednesday.

&&

.AVIATION /07Z FRIDAY THROUGH TUESDAY/...
At KCLT and elsewhere: A large low pressure system will continue to
allow southwesterly gusts to prevail through much of the forecast
period with frequent 20-30 kt gusts at most TAF sites tonight
through much of the daytime period. Some gusts during the day
could exceed 30 kts at times. Gusty winds should slowly subside
by this evening with low-end gusts possibly sticking around past
00Z Saturday. Gusts at KAVL are not expected to be as strong with
a toggle to the northwest by late morning. Low VFR to MVFR cigs
remain in place tonight and through at least the early afternoon
hours before gradually lifting and scattering by this afternoon and
evening. Guidance support a very stubborn hold of the cloud deck
with little clearing until the end of the forecast period. A wintry
mix of mainly snow, with possibly some sleet and light freezing
drizzle in the mountains, mainly near the Tennessee border will
continue overnight. Can't rule out some patchy drizzle overnight
at the TAF sites.

Outlook: Dry and VFR returns Saturday before a cold front brings
a brief shot of rain and associated restrictions Sunday afternoon
into Sunday night. Drier conditions return early next week.
